Package neqsim.pvtsimulation.reservoirproperties.materialbalance

Class VanEverdingenHurstAquifer

java.lang.Object
neqsim.pvtsimulation.reservoirproperties.materialbalance.VanEverdingenHurstAquifer
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class VanEverdingenHurstAquifer extends Object implements Serializable
Van Everdingen-Hurst radial aquifer influence functions and water-influx calculation.

Implements the constant-terminal-rate dimensionless pressure solution $P_D(t_D)$ of Van Everdingen and Hurst (1949) for radial aquifers, together with the Carter-Tracy (1960) cumulative water-influx method that uses $P_D$ and its time derivative. These influence functions can be exported as an ECLIPSE AQUTAB include table and provide the cumulative influx $W_e$ consumed by GasMaterialBalance and OilMaterialBalance.

Dimensionless pressure

For an infinite-acting radial aquifer the constant-terminal-rate dimensionless pressure and its time derivative are integrated from the positive radial diffusion spectrum. Positive log-frequency quadrature with bounded endpoint truncation avoids pressure jumps and finite-difference artifacts at small times. No EOS or history parameters are fitted by this numerical kernel.

For a bounded (no-flow outer boundary) aquifer of dimensionless outer radius $r_{eD}$ the solution transitions to pseudo-steady state; this is approximated as the maximum of the infinite-acting value and the pseudo-steady value $P_D = 2 t_D/(r_{eD}^2 - 1) + \ln r_{eD} - 3/4$. This legacy bounded policy is not a qualified finite-annulus transient solution: it can have a nonzero right limit at time zero and an inaccurate finite-radius intercept. Its derivative selects the active branch; it does not establish bounded radial accuracy. The infinite-acting correction does not resolve that separate physical-domain limitation.

Units

SI units are used throughout: permeability in m$^2$, time in seconds, viscosity in Pa·s, compressibility in 1/Pa, radius and thickness in m, porosity as a fraction, pressures in bar (for the influx $\Delta p$) and the aquifer constant in reservoir m$^3$ per bar. Dimensionless time and pressure are unitless.

    • dimensionlessPressureDerivative

      public static double dimensionlessPressureDerivative(double tD, double reD)
      Time derivative of the selected dimensionless pressure branch, $dP_D/dt_D$.

      Uses the analytic derivative of the same infinite spectral approximation, or the active legacy bounded branch. At a bounded-policy crossing the derivative of the selected branch is returned; that approximate maximum is not differentiable at a genuine kink. Time zero returns zero as a bookkeeping convention, not as its physical right-derivative limit. Used by the Carter-Tracy influx method.

      Parameters:
      tD - finite nonnegative dimensionless time; zero is the bookkeeping origin
      reD - dimensionless outer radius (infinite if non-positive or infinite)
      Returns:
      derivative $dP_D/dt_D$
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if time is negative or non-finite, or the radius argument is NaN

    • dimensionlessTime

      public static double dimensionlessTime(double permeability, double time, double porosity, double viscosity, double totalCompressibility, double reservoirRadius)
      Dimensionless time for a radial aquifer.

      $$ t_D = \frac{k\,t}{\phi\,\mu\,c_t\,r_i^2} $$

      Parameters:
      permeability - finite nonnegative aquifer permeability (m^2); zero gives zero time
      time - finite nonnegative elapsed time (s); zero gives zero dimensionless time
      porosity - finite porosity in (0, 1]
      viscosity - finite positive water viscosity (Pa*s)
      totalCompressibility - finite positive total aquifer compressibility (1/Pa), not 1/bar
      reservoirRadius - finite positive reservoir/aquifer inner radius (m), not outer radius
      Returns:
      dimensionless time $t_D$
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a physical input is outside its stated domain
      ArithmeticException - if a strictly positive result overflows or underflows to zero

    • aquiferConstant

      public static double aquiferConstant(double porosity, double totalCompressibility, double thickness, double reservoirRadius, double encroachmentAngleDeg)
      Van Everdingen-Hurst aquifer constant.

      $$ U = 2\pi\,f\,\phi\,c_t\,h\,r_i^2 $$

      with the encroachment fraction $f = \theta/360$. With compressibility supplied in 1/bar the constant has units of reservoir m$^3$ per bar.

      Parameters:
      porosity - finite porosity in [0, 1]; zero gives zero support
      totalCompressibility - finite nonnegative total aquifer compressibility (1/bar), not 1/Pa
      thickness - finite nonnegative aquifer thickness (m)
      reservoirRadius - finite positive reservoir/aquifer inner radius (m), not outer radius
      encroachmentAngleDeg - finite encroachment angle in [0, 360] degrees
      Returns:
      aquifer constant $U$ (reservoir m^3 per bar)
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a physical input is outside its stated domain
      ArithmeticException - if a strictly positive result overflows or underflows to zero

    • scaledPhysicalRatio

      private static double scaledPhysicalRatio(double[] numerator, double[] denominator)
      Scales a physical conversion only when its ordinary evaluation risks intermediate exponent loss.

      Callers validate positive finite factors and handle physical zeros first. At most seven numerator or five denominator factors keep the normalized mantissa representable even for subnormal inputs. The Carter-Tracy recurrence does not call this helper or allocate these factor arrays.

      Parameters:
      numerator - strictly positive finite numerator factors
      denominator - strictly positive finite denominator factors
      Returns:
      positive finite rounded conversion, including representable subnormal results
      Throws:
      ArithmeticException - if the final positive conversion is unrepresentable

    • roundedPhysicalRatio

      private static double roundedPhysicalRatio(double[] numerator, double[] denominator)
      Resolves final representability near the subnormal and overflow boundaries from exact binary factors.

      Floating scaled mantissas alone can round a value across the half-minimum or overflow threshold. Exact products and integer division in units of the local binary ULP resolve remainder and tie parity without an approximate decimal quotient. Rounded counts are at most 2^53, exactly representable as doubles. This rare path is not used for ordinary conversions or Carter-Tracy steps. The low-end handoff includes the adjacent normal binade so rounded intermediate products cannot hide a subnormal exact ratio. The exact comparisons then select its local ULP.

      Parameters:
      numerator - strictly positive finite numerator factors
      denominator - strictly positive finite denominator factors
      Returns:
      correctly classified final double conversion

    • cumulativeInfluxCarterTracy

      public static double[] cumulativeInfluxCarterTracy(double[] tD, double[] deltaP, double aquiferConstant, double reD)
      Cumulative water influx history by the Carter-Tracy (1960) method.

      Marches the aquifer influx forward without superposition using the recurrence

      $$ W_{e,n} = W_{e,n-1} + (t_{Dn} - t_{Dn-1})\, \frac{U\,\Delta p_n - W_{e,n-1}\,P_D'(t_{Dn})}{P_D(t_{Dn}) - t_{Dn-1} \,P_D'(t_{Dn})} $$

      where $\Delta p_n = p_i - p_n$ is the total pressure drop at the reservoir-aquifer boundary. Evaluation is normalized by positive pressure and uses exponent-scaled products, without an absolute small-denominator freeze. The existing projection to nonnegative cumulative influx is retained: negative total drops may decrease influx to zero, but do not create a negative cumulative water credit. This is not a water-mixing or recharge model. The bounded-radius influence remains the explicitly unqualified legacy policy described above.

      Parameters:
      tD - nonempty finite nonnegative dimensionless times, strictly increasing; first entry may be zero
      deltaP - finite signed total pressure drops $p_i - p$ at each time (bar), same length as times
      aquiferConstant - finite nonnegative aquifer constant $U$ (reservoir m^3 per bar); zero gives zero influx
      reD - dimensionless outer radius (infinite if non-positive or infinite)
      Returns:
      array of cumulative water influx at each time (reservoir m^3), initially zero
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if history shape, ordering, finiteness, support or radius arguments are invalid
      ArithmeticException - if the selected influence or a transition cannot be represented finitely

    • exportAqutab

      Export an ECLIPSE AQUTAB include file body for a Carter-Tracy aquifer influence table.
